_comment: DEFAULT THRESHOLDS — NOT FITTED.
Status: M3 (2026-09-21). Calibration is deferred because no labels exist
yet (SPEC.md §9, M7). These values are documented starting points chosen
to be permissive enough that the system does not reject frames on a clean
machine with no corpus. They will be replaced by threshold fitting on the
dev split once the label campaign (M7) is complete.
DO NOT report precision, recall or F1 against these thresholds: a number
from an unlabelled corpus is not evidence (AGENTS.md §judging-honestly).
Schema: each framing key maps to a thresholds object. The special key
'_default' is used when the shot's framing is not explicitly listed.
Fields per framing (presence):
person_score_threshold: minimum detection score to count a person.
Lower = more recalls (more false positives); higher = more precise
(more false negatives). Starting value: 0.5 (COCO convention).
missing_entity_abstain_on_empty: if true, emit 'unsure' rather than
'missing_entity' when the detector finds zero people in a frame that
declares a character. A blank image and a very-far wide shot both
return zero detections; until we have labelled examples of each, we
should abstain rather than reject good frames. Default: true.
extra_person_confidence: the confidence assigned to an extra_person
finding. Not fitted; 0.8 is a documentation placeholder.
duplicated_character_confidence: idem for duplicated_character.
missing_entity_confidence: idem for missing_entity.
Fields per framing (identity, M3):
identity_similarity_threshold: minimum cosine similarity between frame face
and reference face to accept identity. Below threshold -> wrong_identity.
identity_ambiguous_band: half-width of the ambiguous zone around threshold
([threshold - band, threshold + band]). When similarity falls inside this
zone, the judge abstains (unsure) rather than guessing.
identity_confidence: confidence assigned to a wrong_identity finding.
Fields per framing (vlm_scene, I1):
vlm_duplicated_character_threshold: score threshold for VLM duplicated_character (to be calibrated).
vlm_missing_entity_threshold: score threshold for VLM missing_entity (to be calibrated).
Why wide-shot thresholds are more permissive than close-up:
A close-up and a wide shot must not share a threshold. In a close-up, the face
occupies hundreds of pixels with high facial detail and minimal distortion,
allowing a stricter similarity threshold (0.60) to prevent impostor faces.
In a wide shot, the character's face occupies significantly fewer pixels
(often under 30-50 px), subject to compression artifacts and lower resolution,
which systematically lowers cosine similarity even for the correct character.
The wide-shot threshold is therefore more permissive (0.45) to prevent false
rejections of the true character.
